claims.quote: three girls with CDKL5 mutations showing severe neurodevelopmental impairment
with different epileptic phenotypes and severity

claims.object_text: honeymoon period (seizure-free period longer than two months) as indicator of epilepsy outcome
claims.quote: "honeymoon period", defined as a seizure-free period longer than two months, represented, in our case series, a good indicator of the epilepsy outcome, but not of the severity of developmental impairment

claims.object_text: interictal EEG epileptiform abnormalities, slowing, or disappearance of physiological pattern
claims.quote: even during the "honeymoon period", the interictal EEG showed epileptiform abnormalities, slowing, or a disappearance of physiological pattern
CDKL5 mutations likely play a direct role in psychomotor development
epilepsy is one of the clinical features associated with this complex disorder
currently considered a specific and independent early-infantile epileptic encephalopathy
